messages:
SRE Bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: high error rate and latency on /v1/generate (svc: runtime-serving) — sustained 5xx spike across a narrow set of backends. Auto-pager triggered.
Miguel: oncall here — seeing 500s and token latency spikes, plotting by model and route now. can someone pull kv cache metrics?
Tara: pulling continuous-batching metrics. noticing a big increase in kv-store put ops around 2161234500 (post-deploy). batch window growth correlates with put rate.
Raj: recent tokenizer change landed in runtime v2.1.3 — it tweaks prefix tokenization for template rendering. could be prefix hash mismatch causing regen and KV churn.
Miguel: if tokenizer changed, prefix hashing may create different keys -> cache misses + regen thrash. customer impact?
Elena: CS note — 3 paying customers reported slow responses and some timeouts on chat flows starting ~2161234520. Affected tiers: dedicated and hosted.
Tara: logs show "KV put size" for prefix-cache jumping 8x for some templates. Also continuous batching seems to combine different prefixes because of new token boundaries.
Miguel: immediate mitigation ideas: 1) throttle continuous batching (reduce max window), 2) increase prefix-cache TTL to reduce churn, 3) invalidate affected prefix keys then warm. Which is least risky?
Raj: safest quick step is to cap batching window and roll back tokenizer if we want to be thorough. We can also selectively invalidate keys that match new hash namespace.
Tara: I can push a hotfix to config: set CONT_BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=32 and CONT_BATCH_ENABLED=false for a subset of hosts to test. Will push to canary first.
Miguel: do it. Also add a temporary shard-level KV throttle: kv.put_rate_limit=1000/s via runtime-config.
Ops Bot: Deploy started: runtime-config/patch to set CONT_BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=32 on canary (canary group: runtime-canary-2). Jenkins job #2981.
Tara: canary config applied. Observing canary node metrics — kv-put rate down ~70% and 500s reduced on canary.
Raj: I'm building a small script to scan prefix hashes and map old tokenizer -> new tokenizer keys. We can invalidate only the new namespace to avoid wiping warm cache.
Miguel: good. Elena, can you confirm if CS customers still see errors?
Elena: customers reporting marked improvement on canary-backed flows but still issues for ones routed to older nodes.
Tara: promoting config to 30% of fleet. kicking rolling restarts where necessary.
SRE Bot: Notice: CPU on some nodes spiked during cache regen; tracing shows tight loop in prefix-key generation for long templates.
Raj: found root cause: tokenization change slightly altered whitespace/token boundaries for a subset of template macros -> hash changed for many commonly used prefixes. Continuous batching then combined mismatched prefixes into larger batches causing kv key explosion because prefix+batchID combination space blew out.
Miguel: plan: 1) rollback tokenizer patch in runtime v2.1.3 -> v2.1.2 on production, 2) invalidate new hash namespace (script by Raj), 3) keep CONT_BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=32 for 1 hour, 4) monitor 5xx and kv-put metrics, 5) follow up postmortem.
Tara: rollback image to v2.1.2 started (rolling). Rolling restarts approx 90s per pod.
Ops Bot: Rollback deployment runtime-service -> image:runtime:v2.1.2 started (batch size 50 pods).
Miguel: Raj, share invalidation script please. Put it behind a dry-run first then evict on approval.
Raj: pasted dry-run output below:
```
# dry-run: list keys that would be removed (new-tokenizer namespace)
redis-cli -h kv-cluster --scan --pattern "prefix:newtok:*" | head -n 50
# sample output: prefix:newtok:tmpl:0a3f...
```
Miguel: ran dry-run locally, looks good. Approve delete.
Raj: running eviction (safe delete + rate-limit to avoid thundering):
```
./kv-evict --cluster kv-cluster --namespace prefix:newtok --rate 200/s --confirm
```
Tara: eviction in progress, throttling 200/s. Monitoring put rate and downstream CPU.
SRE Bot: kv put rate dropping, 500s on affected routes decreasing.
Elena: customers on affected routes confirming resolution for most flows. Thanks team.
Miguel: rolling rollback completed, config cap at 32 tokens still active. Observed 5xx back down to baseline within ~8 minutes of eviction start.
Tara: will remove the cap after 30 minutes of stable metrics and then watch for regressions.
Miguel: handing off to Raj for investigation and follow-up (postmortem + root cause writeup). I'm pausing oncall in ~2.5h — Raj, please be primary until then.
Raj: ack, I'll take over. I'll collect correlation graphs (kv-put, prefix misses, batch sizes), embed the eviction steps and the tokenizer diff in the postmortem.
Elena: I'll coordinate customer comms: sent an update to affected accounts summarizing impact (~12 min tail latency/5xx window), mitigation, and next steps.
Miguel: final note: Severity P2, impact limited to specific flows and customers because of template usage. Action items: - rollback tokenizer patch from CI gating, - add warn-level test in presubmit that compares prefix hash distributions between tokenizers, - create opt-in flag for tokenizer changes in runtime to allow staged rollout.
Raj: will add failing test to repo and open PR with rollout guard.
Tara: creating incident ticket and linking config diffs and eviction logs.
Miguel: thanks all. I'll mark this thread resolved in 2h if no regression. :white_check_mark:
